channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Congresso avança rumo ao fim da escala 6x1
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved in two rounds a Constitutional Amendment Proposal (PEC) to reduce the weekly workweek and guarantee workers two days of rest, celebrated as a victory for President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. The approval comes less than five months ahead of the 2026 elections, and the text now moves to the Senate for further review.

item.title: Câmara atropela a 6x1 e joga ao Senado a chance de ser o 'inimigo do povo'
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved a proposal to reduce the workweek from 6x1 to 4x1 with overwhelming support: 472 in favor and 22 against in the first round, and 461 to 19 in the second. Dubbed the 'miracle of the Electronic Ballot Box' by supporters, the bill now moves to the Senate, where it may face stronger opposition. The measure is seen as a labor advancement but also as a challenge to balancing productivity with social rights.

item.title: Eleições e escândalo do Banco Master impulsionam voto pelo fim da jornada 6x1 no Brasil
item.description: The Banco Master scandal and public pressure are driving support for reducing the 6x1 workweek in Brazil. A Constitutional Amendment Proposal was approved in the Chamber of Deputies, with only 22 opposing votes in the first round and 19 in the second, indicating broad parliamentary consensus. Lawmakers are being pressured on the streets and social media to act on demands for better working conditions.

item.title: A 1ª grande vitória do balconista de farmácia que lançou movimento pelo fim da escala 6x1 com desabafo no TikTok
item.description: Pharmacy clerk Rick Azevedo became a national symbol of the fight for reduced working hours after his TikTok rant against the 6x1 work schedule went viral in 2023. His video inspired a petition with over 3 million signatures, led to the founding of the Vida Além do Trabalho (VAT) movement, and culminated in his election as the most-voted PSOL councilor in Rio de Janeiro. Public pressure resulted in the Chamber of Deputies approving, on May 27, a bill to reduce the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours, replacing the 6x1 model with five workdays and two paid days off.

item.title: Lula recebe presidente do Suriname para fechar 12 acordos
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will receive Suriname’s President Jennifer Geerlings-Simons to sign up to 12 bilateral agreements focused on Amazon integration, organized crime combat, infrastructure, and energy cooperation, particularly regarding Suriname’s oil discoveries. The visit centers on four pillars: oil, connectivity and infrastructure, social programs, and agribusiness, with emphasis on police and military cooperation in the border region between Pará, Amapá, and Suriname.

item.title: Zema tenso com o contra-ataque do STF
item.description: Romeu Zema, governor of Minas Gerais and potential presidential candidate for the Novo party, faces internal pressure from his own party, which threatens to withdraw support for his candidacy, along with growing concern over recent Supreme Federal Court (STF) rulings that could impact his political agenda.

item.title: A campanha de Flávio morreu? Especialistas em opinião pública acreditam que não
item.description: Public opinion experts state that Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-candidacy is not over, despite controversies surrounding his relationship with Daniel Vorcaro. They argue the damage so far is limited, reversible, and likely to cause only a 3-4 point drop in polls — within the margin of error — without undermining his loyal voter base.

item.title: As novas modalidades de abuso de poder em resoluções do TSE
item.description: The TSE has been expanding its regulatory power through electoral resolutions, creating new forms of abuse of power, particularly concerning disinformation about the electoral process. Resolution 23.735/2024, which systematized electoral offenses separately from propaganda, innovated not only by maintaining severe sanctions like cassation and ineligibility but also by introducing new illicit figures, such as abuse of power through disinformation about the electoral process, thereby expanding punitive reach beyond mere content removal or fines.

item.title: Governistas comemoram aprovação do fim da 6 X 1 e provocam PL
item.description: Government supporters celebrated the approval of the end of the 6×1 work scale in the Chamber of Deputies, with a PEC establishing a 40-hour weekly cap, two paid days off, and a 14-month transition, negotiated by Hugo Motta, Leo Prates, and backed by Lula. Government leaders such as Paulo Pimenta, Lindbergh Farias, and Marcelo Freixo hailed it as a historic victory for workers, while Fernando Haddad accused the PL of attempting to block the measure. The PEC now moves to the Senate for review.

item.title: PF pediu operação um dia após Kassio pedir vista de julgamento de Cláudio Castro no TSE
item.description: The Federal Police (PF) requested authorization from the Supreme Federal Court (STF) on March 11 to conduct an operation against former Rio de Janeiro governor Cláudio Castro (PL) in the Master case. The request came one day after Justice Kassio Nunes Marques requested a pause (vista) in the TSE trial that could have removed Castro from office. The operation was carried out last Tuesday (26), over two months after the initial request.

item.title: Podcast analisa o saldo e os significados do encontro de Flávio Bolsonaro e Trump
item.description: The meeting between Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Donald Trump was marked by the former U.S. president's silence, as he made no public comments about the gathering — a departure from his usual public remarks with foreign candidates. Details of the Tuesday (26) meeting came solely from allies of the Brazilian senator.

item.title: O fator Trump
item.description: The meeting between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and former U.S. President Donald Trump sparked political reactions, particularly from the Workers’ Party (PT), which questioned the authenticity of the White House photo. Though not a decisive event, the encounter boosts Flávio Bolsonaro’s visibility in the 2026 electoral race, keeping him in the campaign spotlight. The article emphasizes that access to Trump is a strategic advantage, even if not fundamental.

item.title: Eleições 2026: Lula volta de viagem ao Amazonas sem garantia de aliado do PT em palanque local
item.description: Lula concluded his Amazonas visit with billion-dollar investment announcements but failed to secure a unified major ticket with the local PT. Former federal deputy Marcelo Ramos was officially named the PT’s Senate pre-candidate, but key allies Senator Omar Aziz (PSD) and Eduardo Braga (MDB) did not discuss Ramos’ inclusion with Lula, stressing that alliances are built, not imposed. Despite the impasse, Ramos insists his candidacy remains intact and the matter is 'settled' for the PT.

item.title: Diálogo com Alcolumbre, força de Motta na Câmara e ministros de Lula no plenário: os bastidores da aprovação do fim da escala 6x1
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved in first round a constitutional amendment (PEC) reducing the workweek from 44 to 40 hours within up to 14 months, allowing the end of the 6x1 scale, with 472 votes in favor and 22 against. The approval involved negotiations between Chamber President Arthur Lira and Senator Davi Alcolumbre, supported by Lula’s ministers in the plenary, highlighting Motta’s political strength in advancing the agenda.

item.title: Por que Lula não convence a Roberta e o que isso diz sobre 2026
item.description: Roberta, a supermarket cashier in Osasco earning two minimum wages, did not vote for Lula in 2022 and will not in 2026, despite positive macroeconomic indicators. Her belief that the economy worsened stems from the pressure of living costs — rent, gas, credit card debt, and informality — that consume her income even as the minimum wage rises in real terms. For her, the economy and the government are one and the same: a shrinking life produces no gratitude, even with rising graphs in Brasília.

item.title: Lula chama de conquista histórica aprovação na Câmara da PEC que acaba com escala 6x1
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva praised the approval in the Chamber of Deputies of the PEC ending the 6x1 work schedule as a historic and civilizatory achievement, emphasizing progress in reducing the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours.

item.title: Votação do fim da 6x1 é marcada por cantoria, provocações e pastor defendendo mais tempo para sexo
item.description: The Chamber approved the PEC ending the 6x1 work schedule amid chants, provocations, and boos, with a pastor advocating for more time for sex during the debate. The proposal is a key part of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s (PT) re-election campaign for 2026.

item.title: Lula recebe presidente do Suriname nesta quinta e deve assinar acordo de combate ao crime organizado na fronteira
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will meet with Suriname's President Jennifer Geerlings-Simons in Brasília to sign agreements on combating organized crime at the border and environmental cooperation. The meeting will cover Amazon security, logistical integration, trade relations, oil, connectivity, social programs, and agribusiness, with emphasis on forest preservation and tackling transnational crimes such as illegal mining and drug trafficking.

item.title: Fim da escala 6x1: depois de aprovada na Câmara, PEC segue para o Senado, onde deve encontrar resistências; veja detalhes do texto
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved in two rounds a PEC reducing the workweek from 44 to 40 hours, allowing the end of the 6x1 scale. The proposal now moves to the Senate, where it is expected to face resistance due to deliberate pacing and the parliamentary recess, though allies of Senate President Davi Alcolumbre suggest approval before the 2026 elections. The text amends the Constitution to set a maximum daily workday of eight hours and weekly workload of 40 hours, with exceptions via collective bargaining agreements.

item.title: Veja imagens de deputados comemorando o fim da escala 6 X 1
item.description: Left-wing deputies and government allies celebrated in the Chamber the approval in two rounds of the PEC changing the work schedule from 6x1 to 5x2, reducing the weekly workload from 44 to 40 hours. The vote was marked by chants of 'olê, olê, olê, olá, Lula, Lula' and the samba 'Vou Festejar' by Beth Carvalho, with unionists and workers present in the gallery. President Lula and Chamber President Hugo Motta endorsed the measure, which now moves to the Senate.

item.title: O encontro entre Flávio e Trump e os interesses americanos na eleição brasileira - O Assunto #1729
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro met with Donald Trump at the White House on May 26, 2026, securing a symbolic photo and urging the U.S. to designate Brazilian criminal factions as terrorist organizations. The meeting followed controversies over his talks with Daniel Vorcaro and the 'Dark Horse' case, aiming to shift focus from scandal. Analyst Oliver Stuenkel notes U.S. interests in Brazil’s October elections center on security and ideological alignment with the right.

item.title: Michelle aciona STF contra Janones por ligá-la ao caso Master
item.description: Former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro (PL) filed a criminal complaint with the STF against federal deputy André Janones (Rede-MG) for slander, defamation, and insult after he linked her to alleged funds received from Banco Master tied to the Bolsonaro family. Her lawyers argue the statements exceed parliamentary immunity and constitute personal offenses, seeking a minimum of 20,000 euros in moral damages.

item.title: O afago de Lula após avanço da PEC do fim da escala 6×1 na Câmara
item.description: The Chamber approved the PEC to end the 6×1 work schedule, reducing working hours without salary reduction. President Lula praised the measure as a civilizatory and historic achievement, emphasizing workers' right to rest and family time. He thanked Chamber President Hugo Motta and pledged to advance the proposal in the Senate, despite tensions with Senate President Davi Alcolumbre.

item.title: Lula celebra aprovação do fim da escala 6×1 na Câmara: ‘conquista histórica e civilizatória’
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva celebrated the approval in the Chamber of Deputies of a constitutional amendment ending the 6×1 work schedule, calling it a 'historical and civilizatory conquest'. The measure establishes a 14-month transition to reduce the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours, with two paid days off per week, preferably Sundays, while maintaining current salaries. The text now moves to the Senate for analysis after defeating a PL attempt to replace it with a 4×3 schedule proposal.

item.title: Senado aprova isenção tributária para entidades sem fins lucrativos e libera até R$ 2,5 bilhões para investimentos em defesa
item.description: The Senate unanimously approved a bill restoring tax exemptions for nonprofit organizations and allocating up to R$2.5 billion for national defense investments, reversing 2025 changes that had imposed fiscal burdens on the third sector. Senators Flávio Arns and Dorinha Sebra argued the measure corrects a legal distortion that had subjected philanthropic entities to IRPJ, CSLL, and Cofins taxes, with an estimated burden of 2.7% to 4.0% on taxable bases. The bill now proceeds to the Chamber of Deputies.

item.title: Saiba como votou cada deputado na PEC do fim da escala 6 X 1
item.description: The PEC reducing the workweek from 44 to 40 hours was approved in the Chamber of Deputies with 472 votes in favor and 22 against in the first round, and 461 to 19 in the second. The change will be phased: 42 hours after 60 days, 40 hours after 14 months, with two weekly days off effective immediately after the initial 60-day period. Health and security sectors may adjust schedules via collective agreements, while professionals with a university degree and salary above 2.5 times the INSS ceiling are exempt—except public servants, who remain subject to the new rules.

item.title: TV Brasil culpa antena pelo fracasso de entrevista com Lula
item.description: TV Brasil blamed a technical issue with its antenna in Greater São Paulo for the low viewership of an interview with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on the program Sem Censura. The special edition achieved only 0.09 rating points, one of the lowest for broadcast television. The network attributed the poor audience to transmission problems, not the interview's content.

item.title: Lula diz que fim da escala 6x1 é 'conquista civilizatória', agradece Motta e diz que trabalhará pela aprovação no Senado Federal
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva celebrated the approval by the Chamber of Deputies of a constitutional amendment ending the 6x1 work schedule and reducing the workweek to 40 hours without pay cuts, calling it a 'civilizational achievement'. He thanked Chamber President Hugo Motta and pledged to work for its approval in the Federal Senate, emphasizing the benefit to workers' lives — especially women — and crediting broad social mobilization for making the measure possible.

item.title: Câmara aprova em segundo turno PEC do fim da escala 6×1 e despacha texto para o Senado
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved in second round a PEC reducing the workweek from 44 to 40 hours, with a transition period of up to 14 months and guaranteed two weekly days off. The vote was swift, with 461 in favor and 19 against, including many Lula opponents. The measure now moves to the Senate, where the government must negotiate with Senator Davi Alcolumbre, who has had a strained relationship with the Planalto Palace.

item.title: Câmara aprova, em dois turnos, PEC pelo fim da escala 6x1
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved in two rounds a constitutional amendment (PEC) that ends the 6x1 work schedule, reducing the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours without wage loss, guaranteeing two weekly days off, preferably including Sundays. The proposal now moves to the Senate and includes a transition period: after 60 days, the workweek drops to 42 hours, and after 12 months from that point, to 40 hours, with the possibility of extending daily hours through collective bargaining agreements.

item.title: Câmara aprova, em primeiro turno, PEC do fim da escala 6x1
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved in first round PEC 221/19, which ends the 6x1 work schedule, reducing the weekly workload from 44 to 40 hours without salary reduction. The vote was 472 in favor and 22 against. The proposal still requires a second-round vote in the Chamber (minimum 308 votes) and Senate approval (minimum 49 senators) to take effect 60 days after promulgation.

item.title: Câmara aprova em primeiro turno PEC do fim da escala 6×1 e de redução da jornada de trabalho
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved in first round a PEC to reduce the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours without salary cuts, guaranteeing at least two weekly days off, preferably on Sundays. The vote passed with 472 in favor and 22 against, following a maneuver by government leader Paulo Pimenta that blocked a PL amendment seeking a 36-hour workweek. Rapporteur Leo Prates established a transition period of up to 14 months, with two-hour reductions implemented in phases.

item.title: Câmara aprova PEC do fim da escala 6×1; texto vai ao Senado
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved a PEC ending the 6×1 work schedule, reducing the weekly workweek from 44 to 40 hours in two stages without salary reduction. The text passed 472-22 in the first round and 461-19 in the second, and now moves to the Senate. The Lula government avoided supporting the PL’s broader 4×3 proposal to preserve its alliance with the Centrão and ensure political viability.

item.title: Câmara aprova fim da escala 6x1 com jornada máxima de 40 horas semanais; acompanhe
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved in first round PEC 221/19, which ends the 6x1 work schedule and establishes a maximum weekly workload of 40 hours over five days, with two paid rest days, without salary reduction. The proposal received 472 votes in favor and 22 against, and will proceed to a second-round vote. PT deputies praised it as a historic advancement for workers, especially women, while critics called it populist and argued it does not prevent informal work.

item.title: Flávio insiste que Trump trate CV e PCC como terroristas para tentar emparedar Lula na eleição
item.description: Allies of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) are urging the U.S. government to designate the PCC and CV as terrorist organizations, aiming to pressure President Lula’s administration on public security as an electoral strategy for the 2026 elections.

item.title: Justiça suspende projeto da “Times Square” de São Paulo
item.description: São Paulo’s 4th Public Finance Court suspended the Boulevard São João project, a Times Square-inspired initiative to install luminous panels in the city center. The ruling, in response to a popular action challenging the project’s legality, was announced in April by Mayor Ricardo Nunes and Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, and includes daily fines for non-compliance.

item.title: Ganho de popularidade completa mês positivo para Lula
item.description: Despite the scandal involving Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro dominating headlines, President Lula’s approval ratings began recovering earlier than expected, reaching an average of 46.4% in May after a low of 44.2% in March. This improvement was driven by stable fuel prices, income tax discounts, and a more favorable media narrative, placing him in a stronger position for re-election. The consolidation of these gains will depend on factors such as the outcome of the Middle East conflict, sustained economic stability, and the government’s ability to communicate its achievements.

item.title: Motta e Alcolumbre discutem PEC da escala 6x1, mas rito no Senado ainda está indefinido
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta is leading negotiations on a constitutional amendment to end the 6x1 work schedule, following a standoff between President Lula and Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. The procedural path for the proposal in the Senate remains undefined, despite initial discussions. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: STF manda Justiça Eleitoral de Roraima rever regra de eleição
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino ordered Roraima's Electoral Court to revoke a rule allowing candidates to resign public office up to 24 hours after party conventions, stating only Congress can set such deadlines. The ruling impacts the June 21, 2026 supplementary gubernatorial election and may jeopardize the candidacy of Arthur Henrique (PL), who resigned as mayor in April but does not meet the 6-month pre-election requirement. The TRE-RR must now choose between 3-, 4-, or 6-month incompatibility periods under LC 64/90, referenced to the election date.

item.title: Foto e ato falho de Flávio com Trump ampliam desgaste e viram munição para a oposição
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's trip to the U.S. and meeting with Donald Trump sparked controversy after the Brazilian Embassy denied support for a press conference, despite campaign expectations. While the meeting was seen as a symbolic victory for securing a photo with Trump, analysts say the episode was exploited by the opposition to question national sovereignty and alleged U.S. subordination, while Bolsonaro allies aim to turn the image into an electoral asset.

item.title: Deputado que propôs jornada de 52h agora defende escala 4 X 3
item.description: Deputy Sérgio Turra (PP-RS), who initially supported workweeks of up to 52 hours through an amendment to the PEC ending the 6x1 schedule, now advocates for the 4x3 work schedule, accusing the left of insincere concern for workers and blaming the Lula government for allegedly 'breaking Brazil'. His shift follows the PL’s announcement of support for reduced working hours, citing electoral impact in 2026, drawing criticism from government allies for perceived inconsistency.

item.title: Deputado do PT é condenado a indenizar Jair Bolsonaro por imagem fake postada nas redes
item.description: Federal Deputy Rogério Correia (PT-MG) was sentenced by a Brasilia court to pay R$20,000 in moral damages to Jair Bolsonaro for posting an AI-generated image falsely linking the former president to the Banco Master corruption scandal. The judge ruled that while political criticism is protected, distributing a fabricated image simulating a real event exceeds the bounds of free speech. In addition to the fine, Correia must refrain from republishing the image and issue a public retraction on social media for at least 48 hours.

item.title: Opositor de Lula tenta limitar subsídio oferecido em PL dos combustíveis
item.description: Bolsonarist deputy Capitão Alden has proposed an amendment to the fuel subsidy bill (PLP) to restrict benefits for cooking gas (GLP), distinguishing between residential use (13 kg cylinders) and industrial/commercial bulk use. He argues the original bill creates cross-subsidies and indiscriminate benefits, citing past statements by Petrobras’ president about considering price differentiation. The amendment will be voted on in the Chamber plenary after the PEC on ending the 6×1 work schedule.

item.title: O que deve afetar Lula x Flávio durante o recesso da Copa e das festas juninas
item.description: During the World Cup and June holidays recess, the campaign between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro is expected to focus on taxes, social media disinformation, and the lasting impact of the 'Pix scam' and early 2025 fears of tax increases, which continue to damage the president's image. Polarization and the spread of false narratives on social media remain central to eroding public trust.

item.title: As crises internas que colocam Valdemar ‘à beira de um ataque de nervos’
item.description: Federal Police investigations against Rio Governor Cláudio Castro (PL-RJ), involving fuel fraud and RioPrevidência investments in Master, threaten Bolsonarism’s electoral strategy in its main stronghold. Despite Castro’s ineligibility by TSE decision, Valdemar Costa Neto maintains public support, aiming to shift political fallout to the STF. PL insiders admit growing concern, as a Rio defeat would carry devastating symbolic weight for the Bolsonaro family.

item.title: Celebrando o atraso: tramitação do fim da 6x1 é aula sobre o Brasil patrimonialista
item.description: The proposal to change Brazil's 6x1 work schedule reflects short-term politics driven by electoral gains, ignoring long-term structural consequences such as low productivity, high informality, and extreme judicialization of labor relations. The text criticizes the political class for lacking commitment to the common good, highlighting the deepening of patrimonialism and the 'us vs. them' rhetoric as a re-election strategy, which worsens both a social and political 'disaster', as warned by experts like José Pastore and Bolivar Lamounier.

item.title: Governo Lula pode multar iFood e Keeta em até R$ 14 milhões
item.description: The Lula government may fine iFood and Keeta up to R$14 million for violating Senacon Ordinance 61/2026, which requires delivery platforms to disclose price breakdowns to consumers. The measure aims to ensure transparency and protect workers' rights, with Uber and 99 already compliant. Seven other platforms are under investigation, and iFood and Keeta have 20 days to respond before sanctions are applied under Article 57 of the Consumer Defense Code.

item.title: Cinco momentos em que Soraya Thronicke foi contra Lula
item.description: Senator Soraya Thronicke (PSB-MS) announced her support for President Lula's re-election, after having been elected in 2018 with Bolsonaro's backing and maintaining criticism of the PT in subsequent years. She has now reversed her position, despite previously making multiple statements against Lula and the PT, including calling him a 'liar' and criticizing his economic team.

item.title: Fim da escala de trabalho 6×1 com regras de transição avança na Câmara
item.description: The Chamber approved the base text of the PEC ending the 6×1 work schedule and reducing the weekly workload to 40 hours, with a 14-month transition and partial opposition support. Meanwhile, Operation Sem Desconto seized assets in a pension fraud scheme, while Flávio Bolsonaro’s meeting with Trump sparked political clashes and mutual accusations. Minister Nunes Marques launched a review process that could annul Jair Bolsonaro’s conviction in the coup plot case, giving the PGR 20 days to respond.

item.title: Projeto de lei propõe condições especiais para pacientes com diabetes 1; entenda
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies approved PL 5868/25, which guarantees special conditions for people with type 1 diabetes, including public healthcare access, breaks for glucose monitoring in school and work, appropriate school meals, and inclusion of the diagnosis in the National Identity Card. The bill aims to remove discriminatory barriers and promote social inclusion, supported by deputies João Cury and Rodrigo Rollemberg.
